attempted_claim: Let E be the elliptic curve 14a1 over Q with weight-2 newform f of level 14, Atkin-Lehner eigensystem w2 = -1, w7 = +1, and let K = Q(sqrt(-31)) of class number 3, in which 2 and 7 split so the classical Heegner hypothesis holds for X0(14). Let chi be a fixed nontrivial unramified cubic class-group character of K, so the Rankin-Selberg convolution L(s, f, chi) is self-dual of root number -1. Let P_chi in E(H_K) tensor C^chi be the chi-isotypic Heegner component obtained from CM points of discriminant -31 on X0(14) via the modular parametrization with the Atkin-Lehner test vector of f. Via the explicit Gross-Zagier formula L'(1, f, chi) = c(f, K, chi) * h_NT(P_chi) with fully specified nonzero constant c, decide whether h_NT(P_chi) is nonzero, equivalently whether L'(1, f, chi) != 0. A complete answer is a self-contained rigorous proof either of nonzero height with exact constant and chi-component rank-one consequence, or of vanishing height with vanishing derivative, via a bounded attack computing c from the Cai-Shu-Tian local factors and the Rankin derivative from modular symbols to certified precision, with all normalizations explicit.
decisive_failure: No numeric value of L'(1,f,chi), no verified root number, and no evaluated Gross-Zagier constant exist in the workspace; artifacts are empty and the planned AFE computation was never run. Setup verifications alone cannot decide nonvanishing versus vanishing of the chi-isotypic height.
